title: A Zebrafish Embryo Model for In Vivo Visualization and Intravital Analysis of Biomaterial-associated Staphylococcus aureus Infection
protocol: Take 4 to 5 colonies of S. aureus RN4220 bacteria from tryptic soya agar culture plates supplemented with 10 µg/mL chloramphenicol.
Culture the bacteria to mid-logarithmic growth phase in 10 mL of tryptic soy broth supplemented with 10 µg/mL chloramphenicol at 37 °C under shaking.
Dilute 100 µL of the bacterial suspension in 900 µL of sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS) in a cuvette for an optical density (OD) measurement at 620 nm.
Culture the bacteria until the OD620 reaches 0.4–0.8.
Centrifuge bacteria at 3,500 x g for 10 min.
Re-suspend pelleted bacteria in 1 mL of sterile PBS.
Wash bacteria with sterile PBS twice.
Re-suspend bacteria in 1.1 mL of 4% (w/v) PVP40 solution in PBS.
Vortex bacterial suspension.
Dilute 100 µL of the bacterial suspension in 900 µL of sterile PBS for OD620 measurement.
Adjust concentration of bacterial suspension with PVP40 solution.
Centrifuge microspheres for 1 min at 1,000 x g.
Discard supernatant from centrifuged microspheres.
Re-suspend microspheres in the "Bacteria-only" suspension (PVP40 solution).
Dilute the Bacteria-Microspheres suspension with 0.5 volume of PVP40 solution.
Mix the suspensions by vortexing.
Transfer 100 μL of the “Bacteria-only” and Bacteria-Microspheres suspensions to a 96 well-plate.
Serially dilute the suspensions in sterile PBS by transferring 10 μL aliquots into 90 μL of PBS.
Plate duplicate 10 μL aliquots of the undiluted and diluted suspensions on agarose plates.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C overnight.
Count the colonies on the plates.
Calculate the numbers of bacteria (colony-forming units, CFU).
Cross wild type Tupfel long fin (TL) zebrafish or selected transgenic line in a tank with a net added to induce egg production after the light turns on.
Separate adults from the produced eggs.
Collect embryos the next day and discard non-transparent, non-viable ones.
Keep approximately 60 embryos per Petri dish in E3 medium and incubate at 28 °C.
Remove dead and abnormal embryos daily.
Refresh E3 medium daily.
Prepare glass microcapillary needles for injection using a micropipette puller instrument with specified settings: heat 772, pull 100, vel 200, time 40, gas 75.
Break the needle tip to an outer diameter of approximately 20 μm with forceps under a light microscope.
Heat agarose solution using a microwave oven.
Pour heated agarose solution into a 100-mm Petri dish.
Place a plastic mold template on top of the agarose solution in the Petri dish.
Incubate the Petri dish at room temperature until the agarose solidifies.
Remove the mold from the agarose plate when it has solidified.
At 3 d post-fertilization, place zebrafish embryos into a Petri dish containing Tricaine (0.02% w/v) to anaesthetize them.
Incubate embryos in Tricaine-containing E3 medium for 5 min.
Transfer the anaesthetized embryos to the agarose plate overlaid with E3 medium containing Tricaine.
Align the embryos in one orientation for injection.
Anaesthetize Mpeg1: Kaede transgenic line embryos in E3 medium containing 0.02% (w/v) tricaine.
Select embryos expressing green fluorescent proteins using a stereo fluorescence microscope.
Load the needle with approximately 10 µL of the "Bacteria-only" or Bacteria-Microspheres suspension using a microloader pipette tip.
Mount the needle onto a micromanipulator connected to the micro-injector.
Set the pressure to 300–350, back pressure to 0, and time to 2 ms for injections of 2–3 nL.
Insert the needle into the muscle tissue of embryos under a light microscope at an angle of 45–60°.
Adjust the position of the needle in the tissue by gently moving it back and forth.
Inject the embryos using a foot pedal connected to the micro-injector.
Score the embryos for successful infection under a stereo fluorescence microscope after injecting fluorescent bacteria.
Discard the embryos scored negative (no visible fluorescent bacteria or no visible fluorescent microspheres).
Maintain embryos individually in E3 medium in 48-well plates.
Refresh the medium daily.
Score all embryos microscopically for the presence of fluorescent bacteria using a stereo fluorescence microscope starting immediately after injections and on each subsequent day until selection.
Randomly select live infected embryos shortly after injection (5 to 6 in this study) and transfer them individually into separate 2 mL microtubes using sterile tips.
Remove the medium from selected embryos, wash with sterile PBS once, and add 100 μL of sterile PBS.
Add 2–3 sterile zirconia beads to each vial containing washed embryos.
Crush the embryos at 3,500 rpm for 30 seconds using a homogenizer.
Culture the crushed embryo homogenate quantitatively as per step 1.3 guidelines.
Anaesthetize the embryos according to step 4.2 protocol.
Pipette 500 μL of PBS-2% methyl cellulose solution into a Petri dish containing E3 medium with 0.02% Tricaine.
Place the embryos in the methyl cellulose solution for imaging, ensuring they are straight and horizontal.
Use a stereo fluorescence microscope equipped with bright field, mCherry, GFP, and UV filters to image individual embryos.
Set the focal plane such that the tissue damage caused by the injection is in focus using the bright field filter.
Set the Z-stack depth at 10 µm and step size at 5 µm for recording of 3 consecutive images.
Image individual embryos once daily from 5 h post-injection until 2 days post-injection.
Exclude dead embryos (no heartbeat or embryo partly degraded) for further imaging and analysis.
Maintain embryos individually in E3 medium in 48-well plates.
Refresh the medium daily.
